report:
Conclusion: the difference is a domain/style shift toward cooking/culinary language — i.e., Model B has extra activation that pushes generation toward words about cooking, baking, recipes, kitchen/chef/food.

Why I conclude that
- The logit-lens top tokens for the highest-norm cells are dominated by culinary vocabulary across many high-norm (layer,position) cells: Bake/Baked/Baking, Cook/Cooking, kitchen/Kitchen, butter/Butter, cake/Cake, recipe/recipes, Chef, Thanksgiving, culinary, family, etc. This is a coherent semantic cluster (cooking/recipes/food).
- The L2-norm of the difference is concentrated in the later transformer layers (layers ~18–25, especially 23–25) and at the first token positions (pos0/pos1). That pattern is exactly where changes will most affect next-token logits and early continuations.
- Earlier layers show weaker, noisier signals, but the late-layer, early-position concentration plus the repeated culinary tokens across many top cells strongly supports a generation-level bias in that domain.

Caveats
- I did not see explicit patchscope continuations in the evidence, so I am inferring the likely effect on actual continuations from the logit-lens and norm patterns. If patchscope continuations were available, they would confirm whether injected difference produces recipe/food continuations in practice.
- There are a few outlier tokens (digits, a few non-culinary words) in low-to-mid layers, which look like noise; they do not undermine the dominant cooking signal.

So: the evidence supports naming a specific difference — a shift toward culinary/recipe-related output in Model B relative to Model A.
